 This application coming on for hearing this day, the court passed the following:
 ORDER None present for the respondent/complainant despite service of notice.

This first bail application has been filed by the applicant under Section 438 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant, who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Private Complaint Case No.446/2023 registered by respondent No.1/complainant.

On such complaint,
learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Mungawali, District Ashoknagar has taken cognizance for offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 120-B of IPC against the applicant and directed issuance of process against the applicant.

It is alleged against the applicant that he has Vachan Singh vs Tarvindar Singh @ Tilvindar Singh on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164649878/
1 forged mutation register to get his name mutated on the land belonging to complainant Tarvindar Singh at Village Geelaropa, Mungawali.

entities.text: Vachan Singh vs Tarvindar Singh @ Tilvindar Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that complaint was filed by Tarvindar Singh alleging forgery in mutation register dated 15.08.1994.

Complainant Tarvindar Singh has filed a civil suit for declaration of title and possession of same land alleging forgery of same mutation register, which is pending before learned Civil Judge, Class II, Mungawali, District Ashoknagar since 11.04.2022.

entities.text: Civil Judge, Class II, Mungawali, District Ashoknagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Thereafter, a criminal complaint on same set of facts was filed by Tarvindar Singh giving civil dispute a colour of criminal prosecution.
Applicant and complainant have jointly purchased the disputed land, thereafter, on the basis of mutual partition, entries were made in mutation register.
No offence is made out against the applicant.
No criminal antecedent is reported against him.
Learned Counsel further submits that applicant is an agriculturist by profession.
He has family to look after.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving his family and home.
There is no likelihood of his tampering with evidence.
Jail incarceration would cause great hardship to the applicant and his family.
Applicant is ready to co-operate with investigation.
Therefore, the applicant may be extended the benefit of anticipatory bail.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and perused the record.

Cons idering the arguments advanced by applicant and overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Thus, the application is allowed.
